requirements.statement: Every category in a label is one of the 39 categories of the taxonomy, written exactly as the taxonomy writes it.

source: bad.push({start: 0, end: 0, why: 'category not in taxonomy form: ' + c});
detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' category name(s) off the taxonomy form' : 'category names follow the taxonomy form',
means: Checks each category name has the taxonomy's Family – variant form; the full 39-name list is not in the outline, so exact membership is left to the person.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a timecode span, start–end in mm:ss, inside the clip's duration.

source: (text, request, material) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { const s = (+m[1])*60+(+m[2]); const e = (+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if (e <= s) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'span end not after start'}); } const d = text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); if (d) { const dur = (+d[1])*60+(+d[2]); const re2 = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; while ((m = re2.exec(text))) { if ((+m[3])*60+(+m[4]) > dur) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'span runs past duration'}); } } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' span problem(s)' : 'spans are mm:ss, ordered and inside duration', spans: bad }; }
means: Checks each span is mm:ss start–end, the end after the start and inside the clip duration.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries a risk level: Low, Medium or High.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"risk"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { if (!['Low','Medium','High','Floor'].includes(m[1])) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'risk not Low, Medium or High'}); } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' risk value(s) invalid' : 'risk values valid', spans: bad }; }
means: Checks each category's risk value is Low, Medium or High.

requirements.statement: "High" risk requires an explicit depiction in the clip: a described act, injury, blood, a weapon fired, an explicit sexual act. A reference, a mention or a discussion is Medium at most.
A clip labelled "Firearms – depiction" or "Firearms – use" is never also labelled "Floor – all brands".

source: (text) => { const hasFire = /Firearms – (depiction|use)/.test(text); const hasFloor = /Floor – all brands/.test(text); const ok = !(hasFire && hasFloor); return { ok, detail: ok ? 'no firearms and floor label together' : 'firearms label carries Floor – all brands', spans: ok ? [] : [{start:0,end:0,why:'Floor – all brands alongside a firearms label'}] }; }
means: Checks the label does not hold both a Firearms category and Floor – all brands.

requirements.statement: A clip with no flagged category is labelled "Floor – all brands" with risk Floor and no timecode.

source: (text) => { const hasFloor = /Floor – all brands/.test(text); const cats = (text.match(/"category"\s*:/g)||[]).length; const ok = !hasFloor || cats === 1; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'floor label used only when nothing is flagged' : 'Floor – all brands given with flagged categories', spans: ok ? [] : [{start:0,end:0,why:'Floor label with flagged categories'}] }; }
means: Checks Floor – all brands appears only as the single category of a label, with no other flagged categories.

requirements.statement: Every flagged category carries evidence: the words of the transcript, copied, that support it.

source: (text) => { const bad=[]; const re=/"category"\s*:\s*"[^"]+"[\s\S]*?"evidence"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; let m; while((m=re.exec(text))){ if(!m[1].trim()) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'empty evidence'}); } return {ok:bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? bad.length+' empty evidence':'evidence present', spans:bad}; }
means: Each category has a non-empty evidence string; whether it is a true transcript quote is not checked here.

requirements.statement: "Violence – graphic" requires described injury or blood; a scuffle, a push or a threat is "Violence – minor".
"Language – strong" requires a word of the strong list in the transcript; "Language – mild" otherwise.
A label carries no category the transcript does not support with evidence.
Risk is the highest of the flagged categories' risk levels, carried once at the top of the label as overall.

source: (text) => { const order={Floor:0,Low:1,Medium:2,High:3}; const ov=text.match(/"overall"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/); const risks=[...text.matchAll(/"risk"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g)].map(x=>x[1]).filter(r=>r in order); if(!ov) return {ok:false, detail:'no overall', spans:[]}; if(!risks.length) return {ok:true, detail:'no flagged risks', spans:[]}; const max=risks.reduce((a,b)=>order[b]>order[a]?b:a); const ok=ov[1]===max; return {ok, detail: ok? 'overall is highest risk' : 'overall '+ov[1]+' but highest is '+max, spans: ok?[]:[{start:ov.index,end:ov.index+ov[0].length,why:'overall mismatch'}]}; }
means: The overall value must equal the highest risk among the categories, and appear once.

requirements.statement: A span's end is after its start, and no span runs past the duration.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { const s=(+m[1])*60+(+m[2]), e=(+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if (e<=s) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'end not after start'}); } return { ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length+' span(s) end before start' : 'every span ends after it starts', spans: bad }; }
means: Checks each span's end is after its start; the duration bound is checked under step 2.

requirements.statement: Where the same act is both "Violence" and "Dangerous acts", both are flagged, each with its own evidence.
A news report of a disaster is "Disaster – news", Medium at most; graphic footage described is "Disaster – graphic".
A reference to alcohol in passing is "Alcohol – reference", Low; drinking described is "Alcohol – consumption", Medium.
Numbers in a span are seconds and minutes only: no frame counts.

source: (text) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"([^"]*)"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { if (!/^\d{2}:\d{2}\s*[–-]\s*\d{2}:\d{2}$/.test(m[1])) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'span not mm:ss'}); } return { ok: bad.length===0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length+' span(s) not in mm:ss' : 'spans use mm:ss only, no frame counts', spans: bad }; }
means: Checks each span is written as mm:ss–mm:ss with no frame count.

requirements.statement: Evidence is copied from the transcript, never paraphrased.

return {ok:bad.length===0, detail: bad.length? bad.length+' evidence string(s) not verbatim':'evidence verbatim in transcript', spans:bad};
means: Each evidence string must appear word for word in the transcript material.

requirements.statement: A category flagged twice is listed once, with the earliest span.

source: (text) => { const cats = [...text.matchAll(/"category"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"/g)].map(x=>x[1]); const seen = {}; const dup = []; for (const c of cats) { if (seen[c]) dup.push(c); seen[c]=1; } return { ok: dup.length===0, detail: dup.length ? 'repeated categories: '+[...new Set(dup)].join(', ') : 'each category listed once', spans: dup.map(c=>({start:0,end:0,why:'category listed twice: '+c})) }; }
means: Checks no category name appears in more than one entry; that the kept span is the earliest is left to the reader.

requirements.statement: The label is JSON with the keys clip, duration, overall, categories; nothing else.

source: (text) => { let obj; try { obj = JSON.parse(text); } catch (e) { return { ok:false, detail:'not valid JSON', spans:[] }; } const keys = Object.keys(obj).sort().join(','); const ok = keys === 'categories,clip,duration,overall'; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'label has exactly the four keys plus clip' : 'keys are: '+keys, spans: ok ? [] : [{start:0,end:0,why:'keys differ from clip, duration, overall, categories'}] }; }
means: Checks the label parses as JSON and its top-level keys are exactly clip, duration, overall and categories.

requirements.statement: Where a clip's transcript is empty, the label is "Floor – all brands" and says so in evidence.
My pieces run 224 to 452 characters; a new piece stays between 1 and 680.
My pieces run 23 to 53 words; a new piece stays between 1 and 83.
My pieces run 1 sentence; a new piece has at most 2.
The longest sentence in my pieces runs 23 to 53 words; in a new piece it stays at most 83 words.
At most 24 line breaks: my pieces carry 12 to 18.
No blank lines: none of my pieces has one.
No hashtags: none of my pieces has one.
No mentions (@): none of my pieces has one.
No links: none of my pieces has one.
No emoji: none of my pieces has one.
Open on a claim, as my pieces do.
Close on a statement, as my pieces do.
The first word is a symbol or emoji, as in every piece of mine.
Quoted phrases: about 53 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Colons: about 28.2 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Figures written in digits: about 20.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries no more than its length expects.
Nominalisations (-tion, -ment, -ness, -ity, -ance, -ence): about 8.7 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
Runs of five or more one-syllable words: about 2.8 per 100 words in my pieces; a new piece carries about as many as its length expects.
I keep paragraphs to 2 sentences at most.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.

Every flagged category carries evidence: the words of the transcript, copied, that support it.
The label is JSON with the keys clip, duration, overall, categories; nothing else.
